claims.text: Severe plastic deformation will produce surface nanocrystallization and a refined grain structure in the AlCoCrFeNi bond coat.
Surface nanocrystallization will increase grain-boundary density in the AlCoCrFeNi bond coat.
Grain-boundary pinning and segregation will enhance diffusion in the nanocrystallized bond coat.
Grain-boundary pinning and segregation will improve oxidation resistance in the nanocrystallized bond coat.
Surface nanocrystallization will reduce oxidation relative to an untreated AlCoCrFeNi bond coat.
Surface nanocrystallization will increase thermal-shock resistance relative to an untreated AlCoCrFeNi bond coat.
Reduced oxidation and increased thermal-shock resistance will improve coating durability and reliability.
The treatment should remain effective during high-temperature exposure in a simulated turbine-engine environment.
The effectiveness of surface nanocrystallization may depend on operating conditions and the material system.
A lack of statistically significant improvement in both oxidation resistance and thermal-shock resistance relative to the untreated baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
